# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Place or deduce numbers within cells according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness-Based
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns while maintaining connectivity

### 1.2 Region-Bounded Number Placement
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers where each block contains exactly as many cells as its number
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N; duplicates in rows/columns must be separated by their value
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrows indicate which adjacent cell holds the highest number

### 1.3 Crossword-Style Number Entry
- **Nansuke** — Fill blank cells with numbers from a given list, reading across or down

---

## 2. REGION / AREA DIVISION PUZZLES
*Divide the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

### 2.1 Fixed-Shape Region Division
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each)
- **Sashigane** — Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends
- **LITS** — Shade one tetromino per bold-outlined region; shaded cells must connect, no 2×2 blocks

### 2.2 Variable-Shape Region Division
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-regions of equal shape
- **Nuritwin** — Divide regions into exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells connect globally

### 2.3 Number-Constrained Region Division
- **Norinori** — Place dominoes (pairs of consecutive black cells) with exactly two per bold-outlined region

---

## 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Determine which cells to color black (or otherwise shade)*

### 3.1 Connectivity & Structure Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells to form a connected "wall"; white islands each contain one number equal to island size
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells by room-count clues; no two shaded cells touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells; numbers indicate total visible white cells in cross; no two black cells touch
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; circled numbers indicate sum of adjacent connected black-cell groups
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold-outlined rectangle contains exactly one wrong number clue
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill exactly the bottom half

### 3.2 Geometric / Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — Shade rectangular/square groups of black cells; white regions must not form rectangles
- **Shakashaka** — Place right-triangles in cells; remaining white areas must form rectangles or squares
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles; diagonal-number clues indicate black cell counts in rows/columns

### 3.3 Uniqueness / Non-Repetition Constraints
- **Chained Block** — Shade blocks touching at corners into "chains"; each chain has no two same-shaped blocks

---

## 4. LOOP / PATH DRAWING PUZZLES
*Draw a continuous line or loop through the grid*

### 4.1 Unconstrained Loop (Cell-Passing)
- **Slitherlink** — Connect dots to form a loop; numbers indicate how many sides of each cell are used
- **Masyu** — Single loop through all circles; white circles go straight with a turn adjacent; black circles turn then go straight
- **Mid-loop** — Single loop where every black circle is the exact midpoint of a straight segment

### 4.2 Region-Constrained Loop
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop through white circles; within each bold region, loop either turns at all or goes straight at all circles
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once, alternating between moon-only and sun-only rooms
- **Suraromu** — Loop from/to a numbered start cell, passing through all "Gates" in a specified order

### 4.3 Direction / Wind Constrained Loop
- **Nagareru** — Directional loop; wind blows from black-arrow cells, forcing loop to move with the wind
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids numbered arrow cells and black cells; arrows indicate count of black cells in that direction

### 4.4 Connection / Path Puzzles
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching paths filling all cells
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (1 or 2 per pair); all islands form one connected network
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint cells to create walls forming a maze from S to G; circles lie on shortest path, triangles do not

---

## 5. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Place specific objects (lights, snakes, blocks, etc.) into the grid*

### 5.1 Light / Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count

### 5.2 Snake / Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments numbered 1–5 sequentially; snakes cannot touch; line-of-sight attack rules apply

### 5.3 Shape / Piece Placement
- **Evolomino** — Place and grow square-groups along arrow paths; each successive block adds one cell in shape

### 5.4 Symbol / Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill cells with — or |; territory numbers indicate excess of one mark over the other; adjacency limits apply

---

## 6. MOVEMENT / RELOCATION PUZZLES
*Move existing elements within the grid to satisfy constraints*

### 6.1 Circle / Token Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles to give each bold-outlined country exactly one circle; numbered circles move that many cells
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area numbers must equal the sum of entering circles

### 6.2 Pencil / Line Extension
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from their tips; line length equals number shown in pencil body

---

## 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC PUZZLES
*Combine two or more of the above mechanic types*

### 7.1 Shading + Number Placement
- **Fillomino** *(also §1.2)* — Numbers define both the values and the shaded block boundaries

### 7.2 Division + Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells; circled cells (Misakis) must have exactly one white neighbor; white cells connect globally

### 7.3 Loop + Shading
- **Yajilin** *(also §4.3)* — Combines black-cell placement with single-loop drawing

---
